title: Rafram
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav Ashi’s student, as in Ketubot 95b: “Rafram went and told the teaching before Rav Ashi”; and in Gittin 42a he raised a difficulty against Rav Ashi.

Hyman identifies him as the colleague of the later Ravina, as in Yoma 78a: the Exilarch came to Hagronia, to Rav Natan’s house; Rafram and all the Rabbis came to the lecture; Ravina did not come. The next day Rafram wanted to appease the Exilarch (so that he would not be angry at Ravina for not coming) and asked Ravina, “Why did the Master not come to the lecture?” He said to him that he had pain in his leg … Ravina said to him, “Does the Master not hold this of Rav Ashi?” Hyman considers this language clear evidence that it was after Rav Ashi’s death, for in Rav Ashi’s lifetime they did not gather at the Exilarch’s house but at Rav Ashi’s place, as cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 3; and Ravina [Rav Ashi’s colleague] died even before Rav Ashi; rather, he is the later Ravina bar Rav Huna.

Likewise in Gittin 11a: Ravina thought to declare valid [documents signed] in the assemblies of the Arameans; Rafram said to him: “We learned ‘courts.’” He disagreed with Rav Acha (whom Hyman identifies as Rav Acha bar Rav).

He is likewise mentioned in Ketubot 36a and Keritot 10a: “Rafram said: This says…” — and they said, “This of Rafram is a fabrication.” He merited to be head of the academy in Pumbedita after Rav Geviha of Bei Katil, from years 744 (תשמד) to 754 (תשנד), without an era specified here, as cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 4, in the B.G. version.

So it is stated explicitly in Bekhorot 36b: Rafram in Pumbedita had a firstborn and gave it to a Kohen without a blemish; (the Kohen) went and made a blemish in it. One day (Rafram) was ill in his eyes; he brought it before him. He said to him: “This firstborn an Israelite gave me with its blemish.” He forced his eyes open and saw his lie, and said to him: “Was it not I who gave it to you?” Hyman infers from this that he was the head in Pumbedita.

The later Rabbi Abbahu was one of the heads of the kallah in his academy, as in Chullin 49a, where Rav Shmuel son of Rabbi Abbahu (he was one of the Savoraim, who died in year 818 (תתיח; era unspecified here), as cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 4, in the B.G. version) said: “Father was one of the heads of the kallah of Rafram.” Rav Rechumai succeeded him as academy head.

notes.text: Rafram asks Ravina, not the Exilarch, why he missed the lecture: saved Davidson Yoma78a paragraphs4–5 supplies the connected dialogue. Hyman’s later-Ravina identification and inference about assembly venues remain his chronology. Years תשמד/תשנד/תתיח are744/754/818 with no era conversion. Rechumai succeeded as academy head, not king.

The consulted Yoma 78a dialogue has Rafram asking Ravina why he missed the lecture, followed by foot-pain, footwear and the Rav Ashi rule. It does not independently date the exchange after Ashi’s death or establish the later Ravina. Hyman’s academy-venue, firstborn-story headship and Savoraic conclusions remain his; 744/754/818 have no era conversion, and succession denotes academy leadership.
